LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.weakTypicalSet: The weakly ε-typical set consists of positive-probability words at length n > 0 whose self-information per symbol under the iid law differs from H(p) by strictly less than ε. At length zero the set is empty.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.mem_weakTypicalSe: A word x is weakly ε-typical exactly when n > 0, its iid probability P(x) is positive, and |−ln P(x)/n − H(p)| < ε.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.weakTypicalSet_ma: For a weakly ε-typical word x of length n under iid law p, its probability lies between exp(−n[H(p) + ε]) and exp(−n[H(p) − ε]), inclusive.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.card_weakTypicalS: The weakly ε-typical set at length n on a finite alphabet has at most exp(n[H(p) + ε]) words.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.prob_mul_exp_le_c: Let T be the weakly ε-typical set at length n for a finite-alphabet iid source p. Then |T| ≥ Pr(T) exp(n[H(p) − ε]), where Pr(T) is its iid probability.
